evidence.claim: In June 1948, Clintwood elected an all-female town council to serve until 1950.
evidence.quote: In June 1948, the town of Clintwood elected an all-female town council for the period from 1948 to 1950.

evidence.claim: Nicknamed the “Petticoat Government,” the council tackled the practical business of town life: parking, garbage disposal and traffic hazards.
evidence.quote: The "Petticoat Government", as it was nicknamed, implemented change in many areas, including cleanup of the town, eliminating parking problems, organizing a systematic garbage disposal system, eliminating several traffic hazards

evidence.claim: It also organized a fire department and bought a fire truck.
evidence.quote: organizing the town's fire department, and purchasing a fire truck.

evidence.claim: The work drew attention beyond Dickenson County. Lady Astor, the Virginia-born member of the British Parliament, expressed a wish to visit and see how the experiment was going; Voice of America featured the town in broadcasts.
evidence.quote: The "Petticoat Government" received the attention of Lady Astor, a Virginia-born member of the British Parliament who expressed a desire to visit Clintwood to see how the experiment was going. The town was also featured in broadcasts by the Voice of America.
